This appeal is filed by the appellant under Section 14(A)(2) of Schedule Caste/Schedule Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities Act), 1989 for setting aside the order of dismissal of bail petition dated 14.02.2023 passed in Crl.Misc.No.63/2023 by the II Addl. District and Sessions Judge, Shivamogga.

2. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1/State and perused the records.
3.
Respondent No.2 served and unrepresented.
The brief facts of the case of prosecution is that the daughter of the first informant, Lakshmi was married about 4 years ago to accused No.1.
Out of the wedlock, a daughter was born who is aged 2 1/2 years.
After one year of their marriage, the accused by consuming alcohol everyday, used to abuse and assault said Lakshmi.
The accused No.3 used to torture said Lakshmi by taking her caste name, besides demanding for money and landed property, from her father.
She was also ousted from the house.
In this regard, several complaints were given in Mahila Police Station.
There were compromise talks in the police station.
Thereafter, on 27.10.2022 at 11.30 a.m., the first informant and her daughter Lakshmi went to the house of the petitioner, he and his family members did not allow them inside the house.
Rukkamma, the sister of the first informant had also accompanied them.
Later, Rukkamma went back to her house.

sentences.text: Appellant is arrested on 28.10.2022 and he is in judicial custody.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that though the bail application was dismissed on earlier occasions, now the evidence has commenced.
The sisters of the appellant are turned hostile and the appellant is in judicial custody for more than one year and he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed by this Court.
6. Per contra, the learned High Court Government Pleader seriously objected the bail application by contending that the appellant has committed alleged offences.
The offence alleged against the petitioner is grave in nature.
If he is released on bail, there is NC: 2024:KHC:6574 likelihood of tampering the prosecution witnesses and hamper the investigation.

7. Taking into consideration of the aforesaid facts, though the police have registered the First Information Report for the offence punishable under Section 498A, 304B, 114 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code, but the charge sheet came to be filed for the offence punishable under Section 498A, 304B read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code.
The trial has already begun.
The sisters of the appellant turned hostile and other two witnesses are also turned hostile.
8. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, if the accused is granted bail by imposing certain conditions, no prejudice would be caused to the case of prosecution.
(ii) The order dated 14.02.2023 passed in Crl.Misc.No.63/2023 by the Court of the II Addl. District and Sessions Judge, Shivamogga is set aside.
